original_question: For the stochastic scheduling model on an unreliable machine governed by the coupled equations d/dt p0(x,t) + d/dx p0(x,t) = -(lambda(x)+mu(x)) p0(x,t) and d/dt p1(x,t) + d/dx p1(x,t) = -eta(x) p1(x,t), with boundary conditions p0(0,t) = delta(t) + integral from 0 to infinity of p1(x,t) eta(x) dx and p1(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of p0(x,t) lambda(x) dx, and initial data p0(x,0) = delta(x), p1(x,0) = 0, determine the explicit time-dependent solution in the general non-constant case lambda(x), mu(x), eta(x). Equivalently, determine the Laplace inverse transforms of the formulas for p1-hat(x,s) and p0-hat(x,s) so that the full time-domain solution can be written down.
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the paper's unresolved general-case problem for the Li-Cao stochastic scheduling model on an unreliable machine: after the paper obtains only the Laplace transforms of the time-dependent solution in the nonconstant-hazard case, recover the actual time-domain solution explicitly by inverting those transforms.
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct model, writes the coupled PDEs with the Dirac-delta boundary and initial conditions, singles out the genuinely general case with nonconstant hazard-rate functions lambda(x), mu(x), eta(x), and correctly focuses on the missing step that the paper does not complete in closed form: passing from the Laplace-domain formulas for p0-hat(x,s) and p1-hat(x,s) to an explicit time-dependent solution.
missing_details: State explicitly that x,t belong to [0, infinity).
Specify that lambda(x), mu(x), and eta(x) are the hazard-rate functions of the random uptime, random processing time, and random repair time, respectively.
State the probabilistic interpretation of p0(x,t) dx and p1(x,t) dx: elapsed processing-time density while the machine is operating, and elapsed repair-time density while the machine is under repair.
Make clear that the question concerns only the general nonconstant case, because the constant-rate case is already explicitly solved in the paper.

Indicate that the target is the full time-domain inversion of the general-case Laplace-transform formulas derived in the paper, not a broader question about well-posedness, semigroup generation, or asymptotic behavior.

Record the regularity/positivity assumptions needed for the hazard rates so that the PDE model and Laplace transforms are meaningful; in the accessible formulation they are treated as hazard-rate functions on [0, infinity), so nonnegativity and enough local integrability/measurability should be included if one wants the question to be fully stand-alone.
Define the notation p0-hat(x,s) and p1-hat(x,s) as the Laplace transforms in the time variable t of p0(x,t) and p1(x,t).
Say explicitly that delta denotes the Dirac delta distribution.

Avoid asking for anything beyond what the paper leaves open: the sharp paper-faithful target is inversion of the general-case Laplace formulas to obtain explicit p0 and p1, not a larger classification or numerical-analysis problem.
refined_question:
For the Li-Cao stochastic scheduling model on an unreliable machine with general hazard-rate functions lambda, mu, eta : [0, infinity) -> [0, infinity), let p0(x,t) and p1(x,t) be defined on [0, infinity) x [0, infinity) by
(1) d/dt p0(x,t) + d/dx p0(x,t) = -(lambda(x)+mu(x)) p0(x,t),
(2) d/dt p1(x,t) + d/dx p1(x,t) = -eta(x) p1(x,t),
with boundary conditions
p0(0,t) = delta(t) + integral from 0 to infinity of p1(x,t) eta(x) dx,
p1(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of p0(x,t) lambda(x) dx,
and initial data
p0(x,0) = delta(x), p1(x,0) = 0.
Here p0(x,t) dx is the probability that at time t the machine is processing the job and its elapsed processing time lies in [x, x+dx), while p1(x,t) dx is the probability that at time t the machine is under repair and its elapsed repair time lies in [x, x+dx). The paper solves the constant-rate case explicitly and, in the general nonconstant case, derives only Laplace-domain formulas for the time-dependent solution. The sharp open question is: determine the inverse Laplace transforms of the paper's general-case formulas for p0-hat(x,s) and p1-hat(x,s), and hence write down an explicit time-domain formula for the full solution (p0(x,t), p1(x,t)) in the general nonconstant case.
justification: The draft matches the Li-Cao model exactly: the same two transport equations, the same Dirac-delta boundary and initial conditions, and the same interpretations of lambda, mu, eta as hazard rates appear in Gupur's earlier 'Further Research Problems' formulation of this model. The 2024 arXiv paper then states, at the highest level, that it gives an explicit time-dependent solution only in the constant-rate special case, whereas in the general case it determines only the Laplace transform of the time-dependent solution and leaves open problems. So the nearest paper-faithful sharpening of your draft is not a broader question about well-posedness or asymptotics, but the narrower unresolved task of explicitly inverting the general-case Laplace-domain formulas to recover p0(x,t) and p1(x,t).
